payload.title: fix(cli): /model switch breaks terminal + garbles streaming output

payload.author: HUQIANTAO
payload.body:
## Update: Root Cause Found for Garbled Output

Investigated the garbled word-order issue (#2488) and found the root cause — it's in the same `/model` switch flow this PR fixes.

### The Bug

After a model switch, `modelSwitchMsg` handler re-issued `waitForAgentEvent(m.eventCh)`, but the goroutine from the last `agentEventMsg` handler was still blocked on the same channel. Two goroutines competing on bubbletea's unbuffered `p.msgs` channel:

```
G1 receives event 0 → p.Send blocks (unbuffered)
G2 receives event 1 → p.Send blocks
receiver reads → gets event 1 first (WRONG ORDER)
receiver reads → gets event 0
```

### Evidence

SSE logging (`/tmp/reasonix-sse.log`) confirmed the API returns tokens in correct order:
```
R: 'The' R: ' user' R: ' is' R: ' asking' R: ' for' R: ' my' R: ' name'
```
But the TUI displayed: "The user is asking for name my again, play sayingfully"

The reordering happens entirely in our event loop, not the API.

### Fix (included in this PR)

Removed the duplicate `waitForAgentEvent` from `modelSwitchMsg` handler. The existing goroutine from the last `agentEventMsg` is still alive and continues receiving events from the new controller (same channel).

Closes #2488

payload.title: fix(cli): CJK bold (**) not rendering — goldmark right-flanking workaround

payload.author: esengine
payload.body:
Thanks for tackling this — CJK punctuation breaking `**bold**` is a real, common annoyance in Chinese output, and the diagnosis (goldmark's CommonMark right-flanking rule not treating full-width punctuation as Unicode punctuation) is exactly right. A few things to address before merge, one of which is a correctness risk.

### Blocking — it can corrupt code spans / code blocks

`fixCJKEmphasis` runs on the whole input **before** parsing, with no awareness of markdown structure. Inline code or fenced blocks that happen to contain paired `**` next to CJK get rewritten too — e.g. `` `a**中文**b` `` becomes `` `a**中文** b` ``, changing the literal code content. The model emits Chinese inside code/strings often enough that this will bite. The space insertion needs to skip code spans and fenced code blocks (or be done at the AST level so it only touches emphasis text, never code).

### Over-correction — narrow the trigger to CJK punctuation

`runes[i-2] > 0x7F` fires on **any** non-ASCII char, including CJK letters. But `**中文**词` already renders fine — the closing `**` is preceded by a CJK *letter*, which CommonMark treats as non-punctuation, so right-flanking already holds. Inserting a space there just adds a stray space and changes the visible text. Only CJK **punctuation** (，。！ etc.) needs the workaround, so gate on something like `unicode.IsPunct(runes[i-2]) && runes[i-2] > 0x7F` rather than all non-ASCII.

### Fragile pairing

The open/close toggle assumes `**` always pairs up; odd counts or non-emphatic `**` (math `2 ** 3`, etc.) mis-pair. `2 ** 3` is space-flanked so it's harmless here, but the state machine is brittle.

### Tests

This changes rendering with no test coverage. Please add: a CJK-punctuation bold case (the fix works), a non-punctuation CJK bold that must NOT gain a space (over-correction guard), and a code span containing `**` + CJK that must be left verbatim.

Happy to re-review. A goldmark inline-parser extension / AST-level pass is the most robust route, but a guarded preprocessor that skips code spans, narrows to CJK punctuation, and has tests would be fine too.

payload.title: feat(serve): add graceful shutdown, request logging, and CORS middleware

payload.author: esengine
payload.body:
Thanks for tackling server hardening. The request logging (with the `responseWriter` status capture) and the `writeJSON` error check are good — I'd happily keep those as-is. Two things block merging, and one is a security regression.

### Blocking — CORS is a security regression, not just a dev convenience

`Handler()` applies `corsMiddleware` **unconditionally**, so `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` is on for every `serve` run (`cli.go:175` wires `Run` → `Handler`). This server has **no auth** and exposes endpoints that drive the agent (`/submit`, `/plan`, …) and stream its output (`/events`).

Right now the browser's same-origin policy is the only thing stopping a random web page the user visits from reading `/events` or POSTing `/submit` cross-origin. `*` removes that protection: any site's JS could read the agent's SSE stream and drive an agent that can run `bash`. Binding to `127.0.0.1` doesn't save us here — DNS-rebinding defeats it, and the request originates from the user's own browser.

Please don't enable CORS by default. Suggested: gate it behind an explicit `--cors`/`--dev` flag, and even then reflect a **specific** allowed origin (e.g. the Vite dev origin) rather than `*`. Default `serve` must stay same-origin-only.

### Blocking — `RunGraceful` is never called

`cli.go:175` still calls `Run` (bare `ListenAndServe`). `RunGraceful` — and with it the `ReadHeaderTimeout` / `IdleTimeout` you added — is dead code; graceful shutdown doesn't actually take effect. To land it, wire `serve` to call `RunGraceful` with a signal-cancelled context (`signal.NotifyContext` for SIGINT/SIGTERM) instead of `Run`.

### Nice to have

A test or two would help — e.g. an OPTIONS preflight returns 204, and shutdown drains within the timeout.

Happy to re-review once CORS is gated/removed and `RunGraceful` is actually wired in. The logging + `writeJSON` changes are good to keep.

payload.author: esengine
payload.body:
Thanks for this — the core prefix-diagnostics idea is solid and genuinely useful: `PrefixShape` hashing with separate system/tools/combined digests, order-stable `normalizeToolSchemas`, no input mutation, real wiring in `Run`, and good end-to-end coverage. It's a nice way to attribute a cache miss to actual system/tools drift vs. the provider's inherent tail miss. A few things should be sorted before merge.

### Blocking — half-wired functionality

1. **`log_rewrite` attribution never fires.** `Session.IncrementRewite()` is only ever called from tests — no production path (compact/fold) bumps `rewriteVersion`, so it stays `0` forever and the `"log_rewrite"` reason can never trigger. Either wire `IncrementRewite()` into the real log-rewrite path, or drop that dimension for now and note it as a follow-up.

2. **No consumer for the diagnostics.** `CacheDiagnostics` is emitted on the Usage event, but nothing in `internal/cli` / `internal/tui` / `desktop` reads it (compare `SessionHit`, which is consumed in `desktop/wire.go`). As written the payload is computed and emitted but never surfaced. Please either add a minimal consumer (even a CLI/debug line) or land this explicitly as a backend-only first step with the UI wiring called out as a follow-up.

### Quality

3. **Typo in public API:** `Session.RewiteVersion()` / `IncrementRewite()` should be `Rewrite` (the field `rewriteVersion` and `LogRewriteVersion` are spelled correctly). Worth fixing before these method names harden into API.

4. **Unrelated dead code:** `turnCount` / `cumulativeTokens` and their methods (`IncrementTurn`, `TurnCount`, `AddTokens`, `CumulativeTokens`) have no callers anywhere and are unrelated to cache diagnostics. Please drop them.

5. **Scope creep in `event.go`:** the `CompactProgress` constant (plus `Progress`/`Tip` fields) isn't on `main-v2`, isn't emitted anywhere in this PR, and is unrelated to this feature — looks pulled in from a compaction branch. Please remove it here.

The system/tools attribution and its tests are good to keep as-is. Happy to re-review once the above are addressed.

## CodeQL 告警分析：两个均为误报

### 1. Polynomial regular expression — 误报

正则 `/\$\{([^}]+)\}/g`：

- `[^}]+` 是否定字符类，只匹配非 `}` 的字符
- 不可能出现 CodeQL 描述的 `${{` + `${{|` 重复导致的指数回溯场景
- 输入 `${{` 时，`[^}]+` 匹配第二个 `{`，遇到 `}` 立即停止，无回溯路径

**结论：** 否定字符类天然不具备多项式回溯风险，此告警为误报。

### 2. Useless regular-expression character escape — 误报

正则中 `\$` 的转义**是必要的**：

- 在 JavaScript 正则中，未转义的 `$` 是行尾锚点（匹配字符串末尾）
- 转义后的 `\$` 才匹配字面量 `$` 字符
- 如果去掉转义，`/\${([^}]+)\}/g` 会被解析为「行尾锚点 + 字面量 `{` + 捕获组 + 字面量 `}`」，完全无法匹配 `${VAR}`

**结论：** `\$` 不是无用转义，而是正确匹配字面 `$` 的必要写法。CodeQL 对此上下文的判断有误。

payload.body:
我对这里的语义变化有个 concern：这个 PR 现在会在 skill 被解析/读取时，把该 skill 同级 `references/*.md` 的直接子文件全部 inline 到 `skill.body` 里。后续一旦这个 skill 通过 `run_skill` / `/skill <name>` / desktop skill run 被使用，或者作为 subagent skill 被启动，这些 reference 内容就会随 `skill.body` 一起进入当前 agent 或子 agent 的上下文。

我看了一下 OpenCode 和 Codex 的实现，它们对这类 skill 目录的处理更偏渐进式：

- OpenCode 的 skills 是 on-demand：系统 prompt / tool description 里只列出可用 skill，agent 通过 `skill` tool 加载对应的 `SKILL.md`。`skill` tool 返回 `SKILL.md` 内容、skill base directory，并说明相对路径资源（如 `scripts/`、`reference/`）在这个 base directory 下；它不会默认读取并 inline 所有 reference 内容。
- Codex 也只在 skills list 里暴露 skill 名称、描述和 `SKILL.md` 路径。使用 skill 时先打开 `SKILL.md`；如果 `SKILL.md` 指向 `references/`，Codex 的规则是只加载当前任务需要的具体文件，不要 bulk-load everything。实际 injection 也是读取 `SKILL.md` 文件本身，不会遍历同级 `references/` 目录并拼入正文。

所以我担心这个 PR 虽然解决了 “reference 内容不可见” 的问题，但会把原本的 progressive disclosure 语义变成 eager/bulk loading。对于 `references/` 里主要放 API 文档、examples、edge cases、troubleshooting 等细节材料的 skill，一次性进入上下文可能会带来比较明显的 token/context 压力，也会稀释 `SKILL.md` 入口文件里的核心指令。

payload.author: esengine
payload.body:
Good catch on the gap — in headless `reasonix run` there's no TUI layer to act on `<<<NEEDS_PRO>>>`, so detecting it in the loop is the right place. But the escalation needs to be **one-shot**, and as written it's permanent.

The escalation contract (src/prompt-fragments.ts:18) promises: *'This aborts the current call and retries this turn on deepseek-v4-pro, **one shot**.'* Your code does `this.model = "deepseek-v4-pro"` and never restores it — and `this.model` isn't reset per turn (only set in the constructor / `configure()`, loop.ts:217/412). So after a single `<<<NEEDS_PRO>>>`, **every subsequent turn for the rest of the session runs on pro**, which contradicts the cost-aware 'one shot this turn' design (this whole product is built around cheap tokens / not burning pro unnecessarily).

Please make it one-shot: capture the base model, escalate for the retry, and restore it after the escalated turn completes (or scope the pro override to the retried call rather than mutating `this.model` for the session). A test that asserts turn N+1 is back on flash after an escalation on turn N would pin it.

Minor: consider writing a one-line stderr note when you escalate in headless (the TUI surfaces '⇧ flash requested escalation — <reason>'; headless currently escalates silently). The `<<<NEEDS_PRO: reason>>>` form carries a reason you could log. Not blocking.

Also FYI this touches the same `loop.ts` region as #2162 (just merged) so you'll likely need a rebase. CI re-approved on my side.

payload.title: fix(tools): enforce auto git rollback checkpoints

payload.author: esengine
payload.body:
This is carefully built — I reviewed the git mechanism and integration closely and the safety engineering is genuinely good:

- Git calls are injection-safe (`execFileSync` with an args array, `--` pathspec separators, `cleanGitEnv()` stripping inherited `GIT_*`).
- Strong protective guards before mutating: rejects when there are **unrelated staged changes** (won't sweep the user's index into the checkpoint), rejects targets that escape the worktree, requires a `.gitignore`, and re-checks `status --porcelain` after the checkpoint commit.
- Integration is correct: each write path calls `prepareAutoGitRollback` and `if (guard) return guard;`, so a rejection genuinely blocks the write rather than just warning. `null` lets normal writes through.
- Opt-in (gated on `memoryEnabled()` + a high-priority memory + a real repo), and there's a test.

Two things before merge:

1. **The activation heuristic is too fuzzy and can self-trigger (blocker).** `isAutoGitRollbackEntry` activates on the literal `auto-git-rollback` marker (good, explicit) **or** on the looser combination of `git add` + `git commit` + any of `edit_file/multi_edit/write_file` appearing in a high-priority memory's text. That second branch means a high-priority memory that merely *documents* a git workflow and happens to mention `edit_file` would silently switch on auto-committing + the strict clean-worktree gate — a surprising, consequential activation (sudden `pre-edit:` commits, edits getting rejected). The high-priority gate narrows it but doesn't remove it. Please drop the fuzzy second branch and require the explicit `auto-git-rollback` marker (or a config flag). Activation of something that writes to git history should be unambiguous.

2. **Confirm the post-checkpoint clean-worktree strictness is intended.** After the checkpoint commit, a non-empty `git status --porcelain` rejects the edit — and that includes **untracked, non-ignored files**. So a single scratch file that isn't gitignored will block every edit while the feature is active. That's defensible as 'guarantee a clean rollback point,' and the `nextAction` guides the user, but it's aggressive enough that I want to confirm it's the deliberate contract for #2146 and not an accident. A line in the PR description (or the high-priority memory's body) documenting 'edits are refused unless the worktree is clean' would set expectations.

Non-blocking note: the git calls are synchronous (`execFileSync`) in the edit path, so each guarded write blocks the event loop for the add/commit/status round-trip. Fine given it's opt-in and must be ordered strictly before the mutation — just flagging the tradeoff.

Tighten the activation to an explicit marker and confirm the clean-worktree contract, and this is ready.
